elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "will be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"

elements.element: At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer"

elements.element: Conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality
elements.evidence: "by an independent auditor bound by written obligations of confidentiality no less protective than those in this Agreement"

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: "IBM will bear all costs ... unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period reviewed"

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "IBM will have no direct or remote access to Customer's systems or networks for such purposes"
"no more than once in any twelve (12) month period"
"at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice" (exceeds the 15-day floor)

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: "IBM will bear all costs ... unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%)" (more protective of Customer)

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are expressly stated in the inserted Subsection 11.3(e): annual frequency cap, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent auditor under written confidentiality, IBM cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no system access.

The insertion is a concise new subsection addressing an absent limitation; the original unlimited investigation right and the existing notice/emergency carve-out sentences remain effective, so no term is contradicted and no undefined term is introduced.

The retained "Except in an emergency or as otherwise required by law" opener mirrors the existing 11.3 carve-out rather than creating a new substantive exception, and the off-site-response and "or remote" additions are short scoping mechanics that operate in Customer's favour, so minimality is not offended.
The clause also comfortably clears the fallback (15 days / 10%), but as the locked target is preferred it should be presented as meeting the preferred position.
